- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive pessimism.  
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and continues downward too aggressively; cap the immediate drop to match true mean reversion.  
- If sentiment turns positive mid-horizon (e.g., +0.3 or above), model frequently underreacts; increase forecast slope gently to reflect sentiment momentum.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative; apply a small upward bias to early forecast points.  
- When sentiment is volatile or mixed (e.g., alternating +/– 0.2–0.3), model tends to over-smooth; allow for sharper, more responsive transitions in forecast.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 2–3 consecutive days below 60–65), model often fails to recognize it; add a slight upward bias to counteract downward drift.
